encounters.cc: Low back pain radiating down right leg with tingling and difficulty lifting right foot

lines: Low back pain radiating down right leg with tingling and difficulty lifting right foot
The patient returns for evaluation of lower extremity symptoms in the context of known lumbar disc herniation and prior diagnosis of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.
He reports the pain radiates down his right leg and is associated with a tingling sensation over the lateral aspect of his thigh and calf.
He also mentions difficulty when trying to lift his right foot off the ground.
His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is controlled with metformin.
- Split-thickness skin grafting for thermal burns involving chest and upper extremities
- Incision and drainage of perianal abscess
- Gabapentin 300 mg PO three times daily
- Father: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 3 years ago.
On physical examination, there is decreased sensation over the lateral thigh, calf, and dorsal foot.
The patient has weakness during great toe extension and difficulty with foot dorsiflexion, inversion, and eversion.
Straight leg raise test is positive on the right side at 30 degrees.
Ankle reflex is diminished on the affected side.
MRI of the lumbar spine reveals a herniated disc at the L4-L5 level with nerve root compression.

lines: Painful, red, and swollen left lower leg with fever and warmth

He denies any trauma to the leg but mentions that he has been dealing with a persistent foot rash for several months, which he has not treated.
